clue.text: American, busy worker posted in for one away

indicators.note: the word posted is placed in the middle of the busy worker

parts.note: the bee is proverbially busy and a worker in its hive
something posted has been sent

explanation.surface: An American worker has been posted somewhere and is now away from home.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone absent from the place they are expected to be is one who is away.

clue.text: European Society boast reveals goods held by third party

parts.note: E for European and S for Society, both standard abbreviations
to crow is to brag or boast

explanation.surface: A European society's bragging lets slip details of a deal involving an intermediary.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal arrangement where money or property is kept by a neutral party until conditions are met.

clue.text: Man following order spies held inside tank

indicators.note: the spies are enclosed within the letters of the tank

parts.note: a cistern is a water tank
the CIA is the US intelligence agency, a body of spies

explanation.surface: A man obeys orders while spies are trapped inside a tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' here is a religious order, not a command.
explanation.definitionFit: A monk of the Cistercian religious order is a man who follows that order's rule.

clue.text: Male beast and one female in mountainous plateau

parts.note: an ass is a beast of burden
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A male animal and a female wander a high upland.
explanation.definitionFit: Geologists use this term for a compact group of mountains forming a raised block.

clue.text: Italian aristocrat to swindle woman

parts.note: to con is to swindle
Tessa is a woman's name

explanation.surface: An Italian noble sets out to cheat a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian word for a countess, the wife of a count or a noblewoman of that rank.

clue.text: Collusion periodically seen around European city

indicators.note: around signals that the selected letters are then turned back to front
taking letters at regular intervals, here the second, fourth, sixth and eighth of the word

explanation.surface: Signs of collusion keep turning up around a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'periodically' takes the even letters of Collusion, O L S O, and 'seen around' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Norway is a city in northern Europe.

clue.text: Left chosen ground beginning to see monstrous location?

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters of chosen are broken up and rearranged
takes only the opening letter of the word see

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned the ground they picked, which was the start of seeing a monster's haunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges CHOSEN into OCHNES; the question mark flags that 'monstrous' alludes to the famous monster.
explanation.definitionFit: This Scottish lake is famed as the supposed home of a monster, Nessie.

clue.text: Good leaves having rotted — event not to be repeated

indicators.note: the abbreviation for good departs from the phrase meaning rotted

parts.note: food that has rotted has gone off

explanation.surface: Good leaves have rotted away in a single unrepeatable event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good leaves' looks like healthy foliage; it is G leaving GONE OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens only once and will not recur is a singular occurrence.

clue.text: Abstain when whipped and party gives punishment

indicators.note: whipped as in beaten or whisked, so the letters of Abstain are stirred into a new order

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: Refusing to vote when the whips demand it earns the party member a punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whipped' rearranges ABSTAIN into BASTINA. The surface is parliamentary: the party whip punishes those who abstain.
explanation.definitionFit: Bastinado is a torture or punishment of beating the soles of the feet.

clue.text: Explained method used to break partnership

indicators.note: the method word is put between the two letters of the partnership, splitting them

parts.note: in bridge, South and North sit as partners
how is the way or method of doing something

explanation.surface: A method is explained for breaking up a partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge is a card game played by two partnerships named by compass points; South and North are one pair.
explanation.definitionFit: To have demonstrated or made clear is to have explained, as in past participle sense.

clue.text: White bird's energy mostly increased with time

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: most of the word for increased, losing its final letter

parts.note: grew means increased

explanation.surface: A white bird's vigour mostly grew as time passed.
explanation.definitionFit: This heron species is noted for its white plumage, so it is a white bird.

clue.text: Ancient burial site moved to Houston

indicators.note: moved means shifted around, so the letters of to Houston are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ancient burial site has been relocated to Houston, Texas.
explanation.walkthrough: SUTTON HOO is an Anglo-Saxon ship burial site in Suffolk, England.
explanation.definitionFit: An Anglo-Saxon royal ship burial from the seventh century was excavated there.

clue.text: Powerful tractor perhaps one you can depend on

definitions.meaning: read literally, a strong thing that tows: a tractor is one example
a person who gives reliable support

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a dependable person who supports others in difficulty.

clue.text: Annual assessment by marriage guidance counsellor?

definitions.meaning: the US president's yearly address to Congress reviewing the nation
read literally, an appraisal of how a marriage is going

explanation.definitionFit: The US president's yearly speech assesses the nation, and a marriage counsellor would assess the health of a couple's partnership.

clue.text: An environmentalist grabbing me initially to sign pledges

parts.note: an gives the article A

indicators.note: the environmentalist encloses the word me

parts.note: a Green is an environmentalist campaigner

indicators.note: takes the first letters of to and sign

explanation.surface: An eco-campaigner buttonholes me first, to get me to sign promises.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal undertakings or promises made between parties, plural like the clue word.

clue.text: Nasty bug from priest going round company

indicators.note: the priest's name surrounds the company abbreviation

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the biblical book of Samuel

explanation.surface: A priest doing the rounds of a firm has caught a nasty bug.
explanation.definitionFit: A bacterium that can cause food poisoning, so it is a nasty microbe.

clue.text: Welcome letter contains something tasty

indicators.note: the phrase Welcome letter holds the answer within it, across the word break

explanation.surface: A welcome letter comes with a tasty treat enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of beaten eggs cooked in a pan is a savoury, appetising food.

clue.text: Course ahead involving Aegean?

indicators.note: the phrase Course ahead takes in the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: A sailor's course ahead takes in the Aegean.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aegean is an example of a body of salt water between Greece and Turkey.

clue.text: See 13
Son in row over repeated test

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the combination is read backwards
the son is placed inside the row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A son is in a row over having to repeat an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts S into TIER, making TISER; 'over' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A British term for sitting an examination again after failing, a second attempt at a test.

clue.text: See 14
Lady first to encourage and tend soldiers

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of the word encourage

parts.note: to tend is to lean or incline
OR stands for Other Ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A lady is the first to encourage and care for soldiers, like a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tend' looks like nursing; here it is inclining, LEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so any lady may bear it.

clue.text: Lure and net snagged on rocks

indicators.note: a snagged net is caught and tangled, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: rocks is slang for ice, as in a drink on the rocks

explanation.surface: Bait and a net get caught on rocks while fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt or attract someone towards something is to lure them.

clue.text: Mother in Greek island to burn up

indicators.note: the word for mother is set inside the island's name

parts.note: Crete is the largest Greek island
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Mother in Crete is getting sunburnt.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce a body to ashes by fire, typically after death.

clue.text: Unpleasantly moist and adhesive earth that covers two miles

indicators.note: the earth wraps around the two letters for miles

parts.note: clay is sticky earth
M is the abbreviation for mile, doubled for two

explanation.surface: Sticky, damp mud lies across two miles of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Damp and sticky to the touch in an unpleasant way, like clammy hands.

clue.text: Brutal invader one who cultivates land some say

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken and heard as the name of the invader

parts.note: a tiller is one who tills the soil; one gives A

explanation.surface: A savage invader turns out to be a farmer, according to some.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech, 'a tiller' is said just like the Hun leader's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth-century king of the Huns was a notoriously ruthless invader of Rome's empire.

clue.text: Articles about Arab producing divine illusion

indicators.note: the two articles sit around the Arab

parts.note: the and a are the definite and indefinite articles
an Omani is an Arab from Oman

explanation.surface: Pieces written about an Arab produce a religious delusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A mania in which a person believes themselves to be a god, a delusion of godhood.

clue.text: Seychelles island hotel in West?

indicators.note: the hotel letter goes inside the first name

parts.note: Mae West was the American actress, so West suggests her first name
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Is a Seychelles island's hotel in the West?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that West is the surname of Mae West, giving MAE.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest island of the Seychelles group, home to the capital Victoria.

clue.text: John being one learner in exclusive institution

indicators.note: the learner letter is put inside the school's name

parts.note: Eton is an exclusive English private school
L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: John is a pupil at an exclusive school.
explanation.walkthrough: John is the surname of the singer Elton John, whose first name is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The pop singer's forename comes before his surname, so it precedes this name.

clue.text: Something trapped a sort of 22

definitions.meaning: a haul or prize caught, as in a fisherman's take
...-22, from Heller's novel, a no-win situation

explanation.definitionFit: A haul is something caught, and Heller's paradox named a kind of trap, so 22 is literally a sort of this.

clue.text: Evil lurks within tomato plant

indicators.note: the evil hides inside the word tomato

parts.note: taken as written
ill means evil or harm

explanation.surface: Something evil is hidden inside a tomato plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican husk-covered fruiting plant related to the tomato and used in salsa.
